Task: Regressed fraction validation
the workflow evaluates the accuracy of regressed land cover fractions (water, mesic, other) derived from a regression model and SMA (Spectral Mixture Analysis) against high-resolution classified proportions from Sentinel-2. It computes residuals (difference, absolute difference, squared difference), generates scatter charts for visual assessment, calculates error metrics (RMSE, MAE, Pearson correlation), and exports validation point feature collections with predicted and reference values for water, mesic, and other classes. The workflow includes image differencing, bucketing continuous fractions into classes, stratified sampling, region sampling, and statistical comparison.

Task: Detect stadium infrastructure change
Analyze pre- and post-event satellite imagery around a stadium location in Kaliningrad to detect changes in infrastructure using Sentinel-1 VV backscatter difference and Sentinel-2 true-color imagery. It computes the difference between pre- and post-event SAR images (S1_ref and S1_match), visualizing increases in VV backscatter as red and decreases as cyan, while also generating a grayscale EO image from a linear combination of B4, B3, and B2 bands. Outputs include three map layers: a grayscale EO composite, and two change layers (cyan for decrease, red for increase in backscatter), with a title label indicating 'Kaliningrad Stadium'.

The output is a flattened feature collection containing mean values per year-variable combination over the AOI, exported as a CSV table.

Task: Detect land cover change using GLAD and Sentinel-2
Monitor land cover changes in Myanmar by analyzing time-series satellite imagery from Landsat 8, Sentinel-2, and Sentinel-1, along with deforestation alerts from GLAD and fire detections from FIRMS. It computes NDVI and EVI2 differences between two periods using normalized composites, applies cloud masking and confidence filtering on fire data, and visualizes change patterns through RGB composites and difference layers. Outputs include median composites for pre- and post-alert periods, vegetation index differences (NDVI/EVI2), GLAD deforestation alerts filtered by date and confidence, FIRMS thermal anomalies with user-defined confidence thresholds, and dual-polarized Sentinel-1 VV/VH intensity and difference maps. All outputs are clipped to user-selected AOIs and exported to Google Drive.

Task: Classify land cover using multi-temporal Sentinel-2 imagery
the workflow performs a land use and land cover (LCLU) classification for Córdoba, Argentina, using multi-temporal Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data from July 2020 to April 2021. It computes vegetation and water indices (EVI, MSAVI, MNDWI), applies cloud and shadow masking, and generates a stacked composite image across seven time periods. Training samples are extracted from a stratified sample of 1,000 points based on an initial classification mask (maskloop2). Three classifiers—Random Forest, CART, and SVM—are trained and applied to produce final LCLU maps, which are exported as assets. The output includes classified raster images representing thematic land cover classes such as urban, agriculture, natural vegetation, water, and bare soil.

Task: Compute tasseled cap components
the workflow performs three advanced pixel-based image transformations on Landsat imagery: (1) Tasseled Cap transformation for Landsat 5 using a predefined 6×6 rotation matrix (RT) applied to TOA reflectance bands B1–B7 to derive brightness, greenness, and wetness components; (2) Principal Component Analysis (PCA) on Landsat 8 TOA bands B2, B3, B4, B5, B6, B7, B10, B11, computing the covariance matrix, eigenvectors, and projecting the data onto principal components; and (3) Linear spectral unmixing of Landsat 8 bands B2–B7 using endmembers derived from mean reflectance in manually digitized bare soil, water, and vegetation polygons, yielding fractional abundance maps ('bare', 'veg', 'water'). It also demonstrates an HSV color space transformation and pan-sharpening using the panchromatic band (B8). All outputs are visualized as interactive map layers in the GEE Code Editor.
